# Chandrayaan-3: Oxygen, sulphur [...truncated by sanitizer]

answer: The mission's key scientific result was confirming the presence of Sulphur (S) on the lunar surface through unambiguous in-situ measurements [1]. ChaSTE also made the first observations of the thermal behaviour of the lunar surface from the Vikram lander [1]. Scientists from NRSC/ISRO estimated that about 2.06 tonnes of lunar epiregolith were ejected and displaced over an area of 108.4 m2 around the landing site [1]. The Progeny rover's APXS detected the presence of minor elements [1]. A later ChaSTE study measured temperatures within the top 6.5 cm of regolith and marked the first such class of unique measurements [3]. Scientists from PRL and ISRO also showed that the mission landed within a buried impact crater around 160 km in size and ~4.4 km deep [5].
